question: What drag and load slope can a shared passive first-harmonic graphite law generate without a UD source?

objects.definition: periodic U0 plus single harmonic driving a separately assumed internal coordinate
objects.units: energy/atom for U0,A; inverse length for k
objects.basis_orientation: x along prescribed sliding cut; sign of k fixed positive
objects.origin: assumed scalar surrogate informed by primary DFT first-harmonic PES
objects.measured_value: source-rounded rigid ideal static shear 13900/6680 Pa

objects.definition: E=U0+kappa q²/2-lambda A q cos(kx), eta qdot=-partial_q E
objects.units: kappa energy/atom; eta energy*time/atom; lambda dimensionless; tau time
objects.basis_orientation: x positive sliding; F negative for positive v
objects.exact_expression: mean F=-lambda² A² k² tau v/[2kappa(1+(kv tau)²)]
objects.normalization: one participating upper atom; contact factor open

sources.source_status: no graphite-specific bath or stiffness source

assumptions: scalar-cut: use one periodic harmonic along prescribed 1D sliding path rather than complete 2D graphite PES
rigid-PES-transfer: use DFT rigid ideal shear as common proportional peak force per participating atom for ratio only
passive-mode: kappa>0, eta>=0, lambda real; separately assumed mode and coupling, not native UD
steady-slide: x=vt externally prescribed, periodic steady response after transients; no stick-slip or thermally activated jumps
shared-bath-ratio: same lambda,eta,kappa and effective atomic area and low-speed regime across N=7,13; source values rounded

technique_plan.technique: exact rational harmonic balance and power identity
technique_plan.purpose_or_na_reason: verify sign, factor of two, steady solution and passive dissipation
square theoretical rigid shear strength ratio only under shared-bath assumptions
single Debye relaxation; explicitly distinct from conservative static PES
this question is continuum response on an assumed mode, not a counting/clock theorem
contact area, q loss, pressure derivatives and full measured force unavailable

integer_fraction_receipt.raw_count_expression: (13900/6680)^2 from published Table 6 source-rounded Pa values
factor_origins: two powers because same-bath low-speed gamma is proportional to squared peak force gradient

clock_receipt.clock_type: physical assumed continuous time in Rayleigh evolution; not UD event time
clock_receipt.physical_unit_map: tau=eta/kappa in seconds if eta energy*time and kappa energy

dynamics_readout.state_space: x externally prescribed; internal q real dimensionless
dynamics_readout.initial_boundary_conditions: steady periodic solution after transient, x=vt
dynamics_readout.conservation_and_sources: dE/dt from external drive equals eta qdot² plus reversible storage; averaged loss nonnegative
dynamics_readout.projection_and_kernel: cycle average of conservative U0 force zero; phase-lag component of q contributes drag
dynamics_readout.physical_mapping: per atom viscous force; contact transfer to PRL friction and UD map OPEN

known_targets: paired detectable peaks near 21.8/38.2 degrees and weak load dependence; other commensurate signals undetected
fitted_parameters_or_formula_choices: one passive q and coupling proportional to PES harmonic amplitude are assumed illustrative null choices, not fit to measured force
target_exposure.search_domain_and_budget: one one-dimensional first-harmonic single-mode family; no optimization or data fit
target_exposure.selection_criterion: minimum passive conventional control to assess incremental UD value
target_exposure.baseline: published rigid DFT first-harmonic static shear, not measured kinetic response

calculation_steps: Solve eta qdot+kappa q=lambda A cos(kvt); with z=kv eta/kappa obtain q=(lambda A/kappa)(cos+z sin)/(1+z²).
Compute F=-partial_x E=-U0_prime-lambda A k q sin(kx); periodic U0 term averages zero.
Use average(sin²)=1/2 and average(sin cos)=0 to obtain mean F=-lambda² A² k² tau v/[2kappa(1+z²)].
Show average eta qdot²=-v average F>=0 and conservative eta->0 drag vanishes.
In v->0 limit gamma=lambda² eta (A k)²/(2kappa²); differentiate logarithm in pressure and include finite-speed denominator derivative.
Under common lambda,eta,kappa, area transfer and low speed, insert source-rounded Table 6 strengths and square 13900/6680 exactly; ratio is theoretical conditional, not measured.
Check conservative self-source integral of U_second*U_first as total derivative; no steady drag without phase lag.

result.exact_expression: <F>=-lambda² A² k² tau v/[2kappa(1+(kv tau)²)]; gamma0=lambda² eta (A k)²/(2kappa²); dP ln gamma0=2dP ln|lambda|+dP ln eta+2dP ln|G|-2dP ln kappa
result.approximation: under shared-bath and proportional-gradient assumptions, gamma7/gamma13≈4.329888 from rounded Table 6 values
result.precision_and_error: exact algebra; ratio exact fraction of rounded theoretical source entries; DFT uncertainty not quantified here
result.scope: prescribed 1D steady sinusoid plus one overdamped passive mode; no contact or stick-slip
result.physical_interpretation: conventional null benchmark only; no UD-specific residual

verification.method: rational harmonic balance and power identity

counterexamples_and_failures: Conservative periodic U0 or eta=0 produces zero steady mean drag; static angle contrast alone is insufficient.
At finite speed different k*tau spoil a simple squared-gradient ratio even if other bath constants match.
Load slope can cancel through eta, kappa or lambda pressure response; negligible experimental slope does not fix these separately.
limitations: The 1D q law is a conventional assumed control, not a derived UD material coupling.
The PRL full force tables, detection threshold and supplement were unavailable; source-rounded Table 6 is theoretical rigid static shear.
Table 2 corrugation ratio should not be squared in place of force-gradient ratio.
Actual graphite has 2D PES, contact edges, defects, mode mixing and possible stick-slip; these are omitted.
Independent physics review NOT_RUN and physical promotion 0.
changed_dependencies: Sets a conventional passive dynamical null for the earlier static registry/source Fourier candidate.
next_discriminant: Measure or compute common two-dimensional PES, contact transfer and dissipative mode spectra versus load; freeze null at both angles, then test signed UD-only residual on held-out forces.
